w10_P4_001697: The final line of a hoist-test log is a net force in kN, found by subtracting 11 kN of counterbalance from an earlier net figure, with the hoist's lifting direction taken as positive. That earlier figure was a combined pull, expressed in kN, with 24 kN of cable drag subtracted from it. The combined pull came from 10 identical hoists acting together, each supplying the force needed to accelerate a 105 kg load at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under the curve y = 3x² + 0x between x = 0 and x = 1. The hoist drum has a diameter of 40 cm. What net force does the final line show, in kN?
w10_P4_001699: A robotics lab's final energy figure, in kJ, is 1 kJ less than a stored-energy figure that is itself expressed in kJ. That stored-energy figure is 19 J more than the combined energy of motion of 8 identical rover wheels. Each wheel has a mass of 6 kg and moves at a speed in m/s equal to the slope of the curve y = 4x³ - 5x² at the point x = 1. What is the lab's final figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001705: A 61,000 g test block on an industrial shaker table is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under the curve y = 2x² + 3x between x = 1 and x = 4. The force the table must apply to the block is converted to kN. The plant has 9 tables, each carrying 9 such blocks. The engineer therefore multiplies the per-block force by 9 and then by 9 again. What total force does the engineer obtain, in kN?
w10_P4_001706: A 52,000 g cargo cart on a mail-sorting line moves at a speed in m/s equal to the smaller root of x² - 13x + 42 = 0. There are 11 such carts moving at once, so their combined energy of motion is 11 times that of one cart. A 22 J allowance for the belt drive is added to the combined value, and the total is converted to kJ. The line runs 6 shifts a day, so the daily figure is 6 times the shift total. What is the daily figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001712: A 29,000 g sled on an ice track moves at a speed in m/s equal to 2 times the sum of 5 and 6. Its energy of motion is measured, and 1 J of sensor bias is added. Eight sleds run in a heat, so the heat total is 8 times that value. The track is 300 m long. Then 14 J of timing-gate loss is subtracted from the heat total, and the result is converted to kJ. What is the final result, in kJ?
w10_P4_001716: A 94,000 g crate on an airport baggage tug is accelerated at a rate in m/s² found by taking the greatest common divisor of 45 and 286, doubling it, and multiplying the result by 7. The tug must supply the force needed for this. A convoy of 12 identical tugs, each with its own crate, pulls away together. The fleet controller records 12 times the single-tug force. What does the controller record, in N?
w10_P4_001719: A cyclist and bike with a combined mass of 58,000 g ride at a speed in m/s equal to the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 5. The energy of motion is converted to kJ. The rider's power meter then adds 15 kJ of stored chemical reserve, then 1 kJ of calibration offset, and then 23 kJ of recovery allowance, in that order. The ride lasted 40 minutes. What is the final figure, in kJ?
w10_P4_001725: The total thrust a launch crew records, in N, is 4 times the thrust of a single booster. A single booster supplies exactly the force needed to accelerate a 19,000 g test payload at a certain rate. That rate, in m/s², is obtained by starting from 8 times the sum of 9 and 8, then subtracting 28, then subtracting 13, and finally subtracting 23. What total thrust does the crew record, in N?
w10_P4_001728: The final figure in a foundry's press report, in kN, is 4 times a line total. The line total is 3 times a bay total, and the bay total is 8 times the force of a single ram, expressed in kN. A single ram accelerates a 147 kg die at a rate in m/s² equal to the number of ways to choose 4 items from a set of 8. The press hall is kept at 22 °C. What is the final figure in the report, in kN?
w10_P4_001729: An 84 kg load on a conveyor is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the larger root of x² - 15x + 56 = 0. The force required for this is supplied by each of 11 conveyor drives, and the plant sums the 11 outputs. There are 5 conveyors per line, 3 lines per hall, and 12 halls, so the plant total is that sum multiplied by 5, then by 3, then by 12. Each conveyor belt is 25 m long. What is the plant total, in N?
w10_P4_001730: A 21,000 g electric-scooter test frame is set to a speed in m/s found by taking the larger root of x² - 11x + 24 = 0, multiplying it by 6, and subtracting 26. Its energy of motion at that speed is measured on a bench. Then 19 J of bearing loss is subtracted. The bench repeats the run 9 times and reports the sum, which is 9 times the single-run value. What sum does the bench report, in J?
w10_P4_001733: A 9,000 g package on a sorting chute slides at a speed in m/s equal to the sum of 2k - 1 for k running from 1 to 4. Its energy of motion is converted to kJ. Four packages ride each chute, there are 12 chutes per sorter, and 8 sorters in the depot, so the depot total is the per-package value multiplied by 4, then by 12, then by 8. The chute is 6 m long. What is the depot total, in kJ?
w10_P4_001736: A 104,000 g sled on a rocket-sled track is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to 7 more than the number of ways to choose 2 sensors from a set of 12. The thrust required for this is converted to kN. The track runs 5 sleds per session and 9 sessions per week, so the weekly thrust tally is the single-sled value multiplied by 5 and then by 9. The track is 2 km long. What is the weekly tally, in kN?
w10_P4_001737: A 165 kg forging on a hammer press is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the second derivative of y = 1·x³ + 1·x² evaluated at x = 3. The force required for this is supplied by each of 7 hammers striking together, and the press sums the 7 outputs. The sum is converted to kN. The press hall has 10 presses and the company has 8 such halls, so the company figure is the per-press value multiplied by 10 and then by 8. The forging is heated to 1100 °C before striking. What is the company figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001742: An 80,000 g pallet on a warehouse lift is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 6x between x = 1 and x = 3. The lift motor supplies the force needed for this, less 29 N that a counter-spring contributes. That motor force is converted to kN. A 15 kN safety allowance is then added. What is the resulting figure, in kN?
w10_P4_001744: A 21,000 g payload on a robot arm is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the number of ways to pick 2 grippers from a set of 8. The arm must supply the force for this. A cell has 11 arms and a factory floor has 6 cells, so the floor total is the single-arm force multiplied by 11 and then by 6. From that total, 17 N of cable drag is subtracted, and the result is converted to kN. What is the result, in kN?
w10_P4_001747: The final figure in a shipyard's winch report, in kN, is 8 times a dock total. The dock total is 11 times a bay total, which is expressed in kN. The bay total is the combined pull of 10 identical winches. Each winch supplies the force needed to accelerate a 123,000 g anchor block at a rate in m/s² equal to the sum of the whole numbers from 1 to 7. What is the final figure in the report, in kN?
w10_P4_001749: The total a rail-test crew reports, in kJ, is 12 times a daily figure. The daily figure is 11 times a per-run figure. The per-run figure is 27 kJ of braking reserve added to the energy of motion of a test trolley, after that energy has been expressed in kJ. The trolley has a mass of 18,000 g and moves at a speed in m/s equal to the second derivative of y = 4x³ - 6x² evaluated at x = 3. What total does the crew report, in kJ?
w10_P4_001750: A 36,000 g projectile on a pneumatic test cannon is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the sum of 2k - 1 for k from 1 to 7, minus 13. The cannon must supply the force for this. The range has 9 cannons per bay, 9 bays, and runs 2 shifts, so the range total is the single-cannon force multiplied by 9, then by 9, then by 2. Each cannon barrel is 4 m long. What is the range total, in N?
w10_P4_001751: The figure a crane inspector writes down, in kN, is 20 kN of static preload added to a nine-cable total. The nine-cable total is 9 times a single-cable force expressed in kN. The single-cable force is what is needed to accelerate a 136,000 g hook block at a rate in m/s² equal to the larger root of x² - 3x + 2 = 0. What figure does the inspector write down, in kN?
w10_P4_001752: A 111,000 g pallet on a distribution-centre conveyor is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the larger root of x² - 10x + 24 = 0. The drive supplies the force needed for this, plus 28 N to overcome roller friction, plus a further 27 N of belt tension. The centre has 10 conveyors per floor and 11 floors. The site total is therefore the per-conveyor value multiplied by 10 and then by 11. What is the site total, in N?
w10_P4_001753: The total a test-track engineer quotes, in kJ, is 7 times a session figure. The session figure is the combined energy of motion of 10 identical test carts, converted to kJ. Each cart has a mass of 36,000 g and moves at a speed in m/s equal to the slope of the curve y = 5x³ - 2x² at the point x = 2. What total does the engineer quote, in kJ?
w10_P4_001755: The total force in a lift-motor report, in N, is 9 times a single-motor figure. The single-motor figure is 6 N less than the force needed to accelerate an 84 kg cabin at a certain rate. That rate, in m/s², is found by taking the second derivative of y = 1·x³ - 5x² at x = 1, multiplying it by 3, and adding 24. What total does the report give, in N?
w10_P4_001756: The figure at the bottom of a dockside crane's load sheet, in kN, is a 16 kN wind allowance added to a yard total. The yard total is 9 times a crane total, and the crane total is 5 times a single-hoist force expressed in kN. The single-hoist force is what is needed to accelerate a 166,000 g container fitting at a rate in m/s² equal to the larger root of x² - 10x + 16 = 0. What figure appears at the bottom of the load sheet, in kN?
w10_P4_001757: The energy total in a cycling-team report, in J, is 5 times a weekly figure. The weekly figure is 12 times a daily figure. The daily figure is 23 J more than the combined energy of motion of 8 identical riders. Each rider and bike together have a mass of 49,000 g and travel at a speed in m/s equal to the larger root of x² - 10x + 21 = 0. What is the energy total in the report, in J?
